# New renderings chosen in odyssey-118 (Odyssey 24.327–437)

Rows are in the format of the table in `conventions.md` (`| Greek | l | i | avoided on purpose |`).

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ αὖ Λαέρτης ἀπαμείβετο φώνησέν τε (reply-formula, 24.327; αὖ for the αὖτ’ of the Alcinous and Euryalus lines) | "Him then in turn answered Laertes, and spoke:" | "Then Laertes answered him in turn, and spoke:" | "addressed" (reserved for προσέειπε / προσέφη); "replied"; follows the shipped τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Ἀλκίνοος ἀπαμείβετο φώνησέν τε exactly, with αὖ and αὖτ’ both "in turn" |
| τὸν δ’ αὖ Λαέρτης πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα (reply-formula, 24.375; πεπνυμένος of Laertes) | "To him in turn prudent Laertes spoke, face to face:" | "Then prudent Laertes spoke to him in turn, face to face:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο / ἀπαμείβετο), "wise" or "sensible" for πεπνυμένος; the shipped τὴν/τὸν δ’ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα with another bearer of the epithet |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσαντε βάτην πρὸς δώματα καλά (24.361; dual participle and dual verb, father and son) | "So then having spoken, the two went to the fine halls." | "So the two of them spoke, and went to the fine halls." | "they" alone (loses the dual), "the pair"; follows the shipped ὣς ἄρα φωνήσασ’ "So then having spoken," / "So she spoke, and" |
| θεῶν αἰειγενετάων (24.373, genitive plural without ἀθανάτων) | "of the gods, the forever-born" | "of the everlasting gods" | "of the immortal gods" (that is ἀθανάτων), "the eternal gods"; keeps the αἰειγενέτης "forever-born" of the shipped ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖς αἰειγενέτῃσιν |
| ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖς ἐναλίγκιον ἄντην (24.371) | "like to the immortal gods to look upon" | "like the immortal gods to look upon" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος), "looking like" (drops ἄντην); the shipped θεῷ ἐναλίγκιος ἄντην "like a god to look upon" with ἀθανάτοις ἐναλίγκιοι joined |
| ἐκ δ’ ἀσαμίνθου βῆ (24.370, with the bath already done) | "And out of the bath he stepped;" | "He stepped out of the bath;" | "went out of the bath"; follows the shipped ἔκ ῥ’ ἀσαμίνθου βῆ (3.468, odyssey-013) |
| ἀμφίπολος Σικελή (24.366; also γυνὴ Σικελὴ γρηῦς 24.211, μήτηρ γρηῦς Σικελή 24.389) | "a handmaid, a Sicel one" / "an old woman, a Sicel one" | "a Sicel handmaid" / "an old Sicel woman" | "Sicilian" (the shipped 24.211 has "Sicel woman"); "attendant" (the table has it for the plural ἀμφίπολοι and odyssey-113 for a singular, but the singular ἀμφίπολος is "handmaid" in odyssey-002, -004 and -015, which this follows) |
| μειλιχίοις ἐπέεσσι καθαπτόμενος προσέειπεν (24.392–393) | "with gentle words accosting, addressed them:" | "addressing them directly with gentle words:" | "rebuking" (the verb need not carry reproach); keeps the table's καθαπτόμενος προσέειπεν and the shipped μειλιχίοισι "gentle" |
| ἐξαῦτις μύθοισιν ἀμειβόμενος προσέειπε (24.350, masculine) | "once more with words, answering, he addressed (them):" | "he answered and spoke again in these words:" | "replied"; the shipped feminine in odyssey-016 has "she spoke to them again in these words" and drops "answering"; here ἀμειβόμενος is kept in `i` as well; προσέειπε has no object in the Greek, so `i` supplies none and `l` has "(them)" in the table's bracket style (the gods of the next line) |
| ὣς ἄρ ἔφη (24.397, Dolius as the next subject) | "So then he spoke," | "So he spoke," | "Thus he spoke", "So he said"; the shipped wording of ὣς ἄρ’ ἔφη (odyssey-008, odyssey-037) |
| ὣς φάτο, τοῦ δ’ αὐτοῦ λύτο γούνατα καὶ φίλον ἦτορ, σήματ’ ἀναγνόντος τά οἱ ἔμπεδα πέφραδ’ Ὀδυσσεύς (24.345–346, masculine of the shipped lines in odyssey-020 and odyssey-113) | "So he spoke, and then his knees were loosed, and his dear heart,\nin him who recognised the signs which Odysseus had told him, sure ones." | "So he spoke, and his knees gave way at once, and his heart too, as he recognised the sure signs which Odysseus had told him." | "firm" or "steady" for ἔμπεδα (kept "sure"); "at once" kept for αὐτοῦ as shipped |
| μείζονα δ’ ἠὲ πάρος καὶ πάσσονα θῆκεν ἰδέσθαι (24.369) | "taller than before and stouter she made him to look upon." | "made him taller than before and stouter to look upon" | "greater" and "thicker" for μείζονα and πάσσονα; follows the shipped μείζονα … καὶ πάσσονα (odyssey-029) and μακρότερον καὶ πάσσονα (odyssey-033) |
| Ὄσσα … ἄγγελος (24.413, personified) | "Rumour, a messenger" | "Rumour, the messenger" | "Report", "Fame" (reserved for κλέος); ὄσσα is a "voice, report" and the edition capitalises it |
| μνηστήρων στυγερὸν θάνατον καὶ κῆρ’ ἐνέπουσα (24.414) | "the suitors' hateful death and doom proclaiming" | "telling of the suitors' hateful death and doom" | "fate" or "black doom" for the plain κῆρα (μέλαιναν is not there); follows the shipped θάνατον καὶ κῆρα μέλαιναν "death and black doom" |
| ἄλαστον πένθος (24.423; Eupeithes for Antinous) | "unforgettable grief" | "a grief he could not forget" (+ note: traditional gloss, some ancients "unbearable", root uncertain) | "unceasing", "intolerable" (each picks the other ancient guess); follows the shipped ἄλαστον "unforgettable" / "past forgetting" |
| οὖλέ τε καὶ μάλα χαῖρε (24.402, Dolius's greeting) | "be well and welcome greatly" | "be well and heartily welcome" | "hail" (drops the wish for health), "rejoice" (the table fixes χαῖρε as "welcome"); the note says the form of οὖλε is unclear |
| ὦ πάτερ (son to father, 24.373) | "O father" | "Father" | "my father", "dear father"; follows ὦ φίλοι "O friends" / "Friends" |
